messages:
incident-bot: P1 page — Azure southafricanorth: BGP route oscillation detected on private connectivity links (affects Dedicated + Private customers). Multiple withdrawals observed. Pager: @Oncall SRE @Alex Cheng. Incident channel opened.
Oncall SRE: Ack — I'm on it. Triage started. Confirming scope of affected prefixes and which customers report errors.
Oncall SRE: Initial check: BGP session to Azure PE shows frequent updates/withdraws. Can't reach some onprem tunnels intermittently. Collecting bgp summary.
Oncall SRE: ```
# show bgp summary
Neighbor        AS      MsgRcv  MsgSent  Up/Down   State/PfxRcd
10.10.1.1       12076   4231    4229     00:42:10  124
203.0.113.5     12076   5240    5238     00:42:05  0 (flapping)
``` 
Maria García: seeing withdraws every ~20-40s for a subset of customer prefixes coming out of Azure. Looks like route churn from the Microsoft edge. Opening Azure support case: MS-INC-56291.
Alex Cheng: Are we sure this is a Microsoft-side instability and not a config loop on our side? Check for recent config pushes.
Oncall SRE: No config pushes in last 24h to the peering policies. Confirmed by eng-releases audit. Likely upstream/peering instability.
Network Ops Bot: Cross-checking telemetry — spike in BGP update rate and transient reachability loss in southafricanorth POPs. Correlates with our private-connect peering timestamps.
Alex Cheng: Mitigation options: 1) Temporarily bump local-pref on alternate egress so customer traffic prefers a stable region (west europe) 2) Advertise more specific prefixes to prefer our transit path 3) Engage Azure to patch on their edge.
Oncall SRE: Implementing temporary local-pref change for affected prefixes to prefer ALT-EGRESS (localpref 200). Applying via config push now.
Oncall SRE: ```
# bgp-policy apply
set policy route-map PREFER-ALT match prefix-list AFFECTED
set policy route-map PREFER-ALT set local-preference 200
commit
``` 
Oncall SRE: Applied. Monitoring for traffic shift.
Oncall SRE: Quick verification pings to customer edge (10.45.0.0/16):
```
PING 10.45.0.1: loss 0% (was 20% before), avg latency 28ms
``` 
Maria García: Good — metrics show a ~70% reduction in packet loss after localpref change. BGP update rate decreased but still above baseline. Azure case open and escalated to their network team.
Sara (Support): Preparing customer notifications. Sending to affected customers in Dedicated/Private in this region. Draft message below — please review.
Sara (Support): "Hi — we're experiencing intermittent connectivity issues to our southafricanorth private endpoints. Our engineering team applied a temporary routing mitigation and traffic should be more stable now. We're monitoring and will follow up with a timeline and root cause. If you see continued issues please reply and we'll prioritize your case. — Redwood Support"
Oncall SRE: Sending to the impacted customer list now (IDs: C-1293, C-1401, C-1420). Also tagging account execs for high-touch customers.
John C-S: I can take the night shift on this one. Handover at 23:00 UTC. Current status: mitigation applied (localpref), partial restoration verified, Azure investigating. Anything specific for me to watch?
Oncall SRE: Monitor BGP update rate and packet loss on affected prefixes. If withdraws resume at previous rate, revert traffic to default and contact Azure Tier 2. Also confirm no regression from localpref change for other regions.
Alex Cheng: File for post-incident: capture BGP dump, config diff, Azure SR number (MS-INC-56291), list of impacted customer sessions, and timeline of mitigation. I'll start the postmortem template.
Network Ops Bot: Alert: Azure case MS-INC-56291 updated — MS Tier 2 is investigating suspected edge maintenance causing route flaps. ETA 3h for update.
Sara (Support): Sent initial customer messages and created support tickets for each impacted customer. Will update when we have an Azure ticket update.
Oncall SRE: Current severity: P1 (customer impact: degraded connectivity/timeouts for on-prem private-connected workloads). Next update in 30m unless status changes. Handoff to @John C-S at 23:00 UTC. Oncall SRE out for now.
John C-S: Taking over. Will keep channel updated every hour or immediately on major change. Leaving a note: watch for any routes unexpectedly suppressed by RPKI/filters after Azure fix.
incident-bot: Incident P1 -> acknowledged by Oncall SRE. SLA timer started: 4h to full mitigation target.
Oncall SRE: Final note before handoff — mitigation reduced customer-visible errors substantially but not fully eliminated. Plan: keep localpref mitigation for next 3h, coordinate with Azure for permanent fix, prepare rollback plan if localpref causes any regressions. Postmortem to follow.
John C-S: Acknowledged. Monitoring live metrics now.
